CVE-2018-25445.title: Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string
CVE-2018-25445.description:
Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

decode_jwt runs the verify_iss, verify_sub, verify_aud and verify_jti checks only when the token carries the claim, and honours an option only as a Regexp or CODE reference. Any other value, such as verify_aud => 'myapp', is ignored.

An application that relies on these checks accepts a validly signed token meant for a different issuer, subject or audience.

CVE-2026-117666.title: ssl_verify_fun: partial-label wildcard certificate matches hostnames across a label boundary
CVE-2026-117666.description:
Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch vulnerability in deadtrickster ssl_verify_fun allows an adversary in the middle to impersonate a TLS peer via a certificate that carries a partial-label wildcard. try_match_wildcard/4 in src/ssl_verify_hostname.erl anchors only the text before and after the * of an identifier such as f*.example.net, so the wildcard also consumes dots and the certificate is accepted for f.evil.example.net. RFC 6125 confines a wildcard to the left-most label. The same matcher lets *.168.1.1 match the IP literal 192.168.1.1. Whole-label wildcards are matched correctly.

Erlang/OTP 20.0 and later check the hostname in ssl before a user verify_fun sees valid_peer, so a client that keeps server_name_indication set rejects the mismatch regardless. Exposed are clients that disable SNI, servers that verify client certificate hostnames with this library, and direct callers of verify_cert_hostname/2.

This issue affects ssl_verify_fun: from 1.0.1 before 1.1.8.

CVE-2026-129289.title: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body
CVE-2026-129289.description:
PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-133776.description:
The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. When the sanitizer changes an icon, it writes the icon out again as HTML. HTML writes the content of some elements, like <style>, without escaping it. But inside an <svg>, browsers parse the content of a <style> element as markup. Escaped markup in such an element then becomes live in the page:

<path onclick="x"/><style xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"><img src=x onerror=alert(1)></style>

The event handler of the <path> element only makes the sanitizer change the icon. Depending on the version, this affects every <style> element, or the elements of the XHTML namespace, like <style>, <xmp> or <noembed>.

On 2.x, the elements of the XHTML namespace were also kept. An XHTML <form> or <base> element then becomes live where icons are parsed as XML, like in the Google Maps bridge of ux-map.

CVE-2026-92549.description: The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'design' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. The vulnerable endpoint is reached via the ?subscribe-preview=true query parameter, which is processed on template_redirect with no capability or nonce check, making it accessible to unauthenticated users.

affected.product: Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress

CVE-2026-99463.title: mm/rmap: don't discard lazyfree THPs at PMD level
CVE-2026-99463.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/rmap: don't discard lazyfree THPs at PMD level

__discard_anon_folio_pmd_locked() clears a lazyfree THP's PMD before it
determines whether the folio can be discarded, and restores it if the
folio is dirty or has extra references. It is done under only the PMD
lock and the anon_vma read lock inside try_to_unmap_one() and no mmap lock
is held. The temporarily none PMD causes UAF.

A parallel munmap() or mremap() is supposed to serialize with it on the
PMD lock, but zap_pmd_range() (called by munmap()) and move_page_tables()
(called by mremap()) do not take the lock when they see the temporarily
none PMD and skip the PMD. There is no more page table walk after the
none PMD is restored:

- munmap(): free_pgtables() waits in unlink_anon_vmas() for the anon_vma
lock, then free_pmd_range() drops the restored PMD as bad without
removing the rmap, so the folio keeps a stale mapcount.

- whole-VMA MREMAP_DONTUNMAP:…

CVE-2026-99584.title: f2fs: fix to avoid folio->mapping dereference in is_{meta, node}_folio()
CVE-2026-99584.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

f2fs: fix to avoid folio->mapping dereference in is_{meta, node}_folio()

Otherwise, it may cause NULL pointer dereference in race condition:

Thread A Thread B
- f2fs_setattr
- f2fs_truncate
- f2fs_truncate_blocks
- f2fs_do_truncate_blocks
- f2fs_truncate_inode_blocks
- truncate_dnode
- truncate_node
- invalidate_mapping_pages
- folio->mapping = NULL
- folio_lock
- is_node_folio
- F2FS_F_SB(folio): dereference on folio->mapping

CVE-2026-99607.title: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes
CVE-2026-99607.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes

ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that may extend i_size,
but clears the flag after ext2_get_blocks(). When the write uses an
existing mapped block, iomap can then use FUA and skip
generic_write_sync(), even though ext2_dio_write_end_io() updates the
inode size. An O_DSYNC write can therefore return without persisting
the new size.

For example, on a FUA-capable device, a 512-byte O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC write
at offset 512 into a fsynced one-byte file returns successfully and
extends the in-memory size to 1024, while an immediate read of the
on-disk inode still shows size 1. An explicit fsync persists the new
size.

Move setting of IOMAP_F_DIRTY after the initialization.
